seoTitle: Hide Indicator Names in TradingView for a Clean Chart
metaDescription: Learn how to hide indicator names and labels in TradingView, manage the settings panel, and keep values visible while cleaning up your chart layout.
intro: A chart cluttered with indicator names and labels can make it harder to focus on price action. This guide shows how to hide indicator titles in TradingView while still keeping the underlying values visible, using the indicator settings panel. It's aimed at traders who want a cleaner, more minimal chart setup.

steps.heading: Open indicator settings
steps.body: Click on the indicator you want to adjust and open its settings panel to access display options.

steps.heading: Hide the title and arguments
steps.body: Within the settings, toggle off the options that display the indicator's title and its input arguments on the chart.

steps.heading: Manage the indicator labels panel
steps.body: Use the visibility toggles in the settings panel to control which labels appear directly on your chart.

steps.heading: Keep values visible while hiding the title
steps.body: You can typically hide the name label while still keeping numeric values displayed, depending on the specific indicator's settings options.

steps.heading: Apply tips for a clean, minimal chart
steps.body: Repeat this process for each indicator on your chart to keep the overall layout uncluttered and easier to read.

faq.question: Will hiding the indicator name affect how it functions?
faq.answer: No, hiding the name or label only changes what's displayed visually and doesn't change how the indicator calculates or behaves.

faq.question: Can I hide labels for all indicators at once?
faq.answer: You generally need to adjust the display settings for each indicator individually rather than applying one setting to all of them at once.

faq.question: Does this setting reset when I reload TradingView?
faq.answer: If you save your layout after making the change, the hidden labels should persist the next time you open that chart.

faq.question: Why would I want to hide indicator names?
faq.answer: Hiding names reduces visual clutter, especially when running multiple indicators, making it easier to focus on price and key signals.
